candidates.title: Plant efficiency: a sensitivity analysis of the capacity factor for fusion power plants with high recirculated power
candidates.notes: Peer-reviewed (Nuclear Fusion Vol. 61, 2021). Directly addresses capacity factor and its interaction with recirculated power fraction — the central challenge for NBI-heavy beam-driven fusion like TAE's Da Vinci. Not FRC-specific but directly applicable by analogy. Analyzes Power Plant Conceptual Study models. Argues first-generation plants will combine high recirculating power with low capacity factor, resulting in poor plant efficiency.

candidates.title: The Princeton Field-Reversed Configuration for Compact Nuclear Fusion Power Plants
candidates.notes: Princeton FRC paper covers D-He3 fuel at 1-10 MW scale (not p-B11, not Da Vinci scale). Steady-state FRC design but no capacity factor data in abstract. Deprioritized.

candidates.title: TAE shortens device roadmap, prepares for commercial era
candidates.notes: TAE's own press release — likely JS-heavy landing page with no quantitative capacity factor data. Deprioritized given no TAE availability claims appear anywhere in public record.

gaps_attempted.notes: No TAE-specific capacity factor data found anywhere in public record. Extracted a peer-reviewed analogy source (Mulder et al. 2021) that directly models the capacity factor penalty for fusion plants with high recirculated power fraction — the core issue for Da Vinci's NBI-driven design. This provides an analytical framework for estimating capacity factor impact, but does not provide a TAE-stated target.

The p-B11 fusion literature confirms B-11 abundance and low fuel cost conceptually but does not provide enrichment cost figures. The analysis's own 'negligible' estimate appears consistent with publicly available qualitative statements. Gap remains open but low-priority nature means this outcome is acceptable.
